source_evidence.observation: The input format has precision t, exponent range [e_min,e_max], u=2^(-t), f_min=2^(e_min), f_max=2^(e_max)(2-2u), and underflow parameter g_min=f_min/2 without subnormals or u f_min with gradual underflow. The accumulation format has T>=t, a containing exponent range, U=2^(-T), analogous F_min and F_max, and G_min. Assuming no overflow, input rounding obeys fl(x)=x(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, and eta delta=0.

Accumulation-format operations obey FL(x op y)=(x op y)(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=U, |eta|<=G_min, eta delta=0, and op in {+,-,multiplication,division}. The default model is round-to-nearest; directed rounding requires replacing u,g_min,U,G_min by twice those quantities.

A is m by n, B is n by q, and the exact target is C=AB. Lambda and M are nonsingular diagonal scaling matrices. Their entries are powers of two so scaling introduces no rounding, and the surrounding computation assumes no underflow or overflow before scaling or after unscaling.

A, B, and C are assumed exactly representable in a sufficiently high-precision storage format. The selected scale is theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)). For a nonzero row x and column y, the maximal power-of-two factors satisfy theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity and theta/(2||y||_infinity)<mu<=theta/||y||_infinity.

The paper introduces a lesssim bound by calling it a simplified version obtained by dropping second-order terms. It supplies no quantified constant, asymptotic variable, or formal definition of lesssim.

p is the number of low-precision words. The retained matrix products are the p(p+1)/2 pairs with i+j<p. The narrow-range variant rescales each residual before input-format rounding: w^(i)=fl((w-sum_{j=0}^{i-1}u^j w^(j))/u^i), for i=0,...,p-1.
The scaled decomposition is applied elementwise to Lambda A and BM. The paper derives, rather than assumes, componentwise residual bounds ending with |Delta x^(p-1)|<=max(u^p|lambda x|,u^(p-1)g_min).

The derived matrix decompositions are A=sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i Lambda^(-1)A^(i)+Delta A and B=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}u^j B^(j)M^(-1)+Delta B, with ||Delta A||_infinity<=zeta||A||_infinity, ||Delta B||_infinity<=zeta||B||_infinity, and zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min).

The paper introduces proof-only errors Delta C and E and rewrites the computed output as the full p-by-p product sum minus omitted pairs i+j>=p, plus accumulation error. The exact decomposition ends with hat C=AB+E.
The omitted-product contribution satisfies a lesssim estimate with displayed coefficient (p-1)u^p multiplying ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity.

The accumulation estimate is printed as ||Delta C||_infinity lesssim ((n+p^2)U+4rn theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity, with r<=np(p+1)/2. The resulting total-error estimate has coefficient 2zeta+zeta^2+(p-1)u^p+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min.

The theorem specifies power-of-two diagonal scaling, input-format p-word residual rounding, and the triangular product sum Lambda^(-1)(sum_{i+j<p}u^(i+j)A^(i)B^(j))M^(-1). It explicitly says that inner products in A^(i)B^(j) are computed in the accumulation format.
Theorem 4.1 gives the four-term coefficient (p+1)u^p + 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min + (n+p^2)U + 2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min in a normwise lesssim forward-error bound.
The range-unrestricted comparison retains only (p+1)u^p and (n+p^2)U.

The paper identifies u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min and theta^(-2)G_min as the additional input- and accumulation-underflow orders. It says the two input-format terms are both reduced from the single-word case by a factor of order u^(p-1).

binders: A in R^(m x n), B in R^(n x q), and the exact target AB in R^(m x q); m,n,q are dimension parameters and n is the common inner dimension. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1]

p is the number of words, with word indices i,j in {0,...,p-1}; positivity and integrality of p are implicit in the phrase p-word and these index ranges, not separately stated. [PDF p. 8, printed B792, multiword definition and eqs. (4.1)-(4.3)]
The input-format parameters are t,e_min,e_max,u,f_min,f_max,g_min, and the accumulation-format parameters are T,E_min,E_max,U,F_min,F_max,G_min. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1 and eqs. (2.1)-(2.2)]
Lambda and M are dimension-compatible diagonal power-of-two scaling matrices; A^(i) and B^(j) are the computed input-format words. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1 and eqs. (4.29)-(4.30)]
Delta A, Delta B, Delta C, zeta, r, and E are proof quantities or error aggregates; they are not additional algorithm inputs. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.18)-(4.28)]

hat C is the computed output, while AB is the exact real matrix product. The symbol C is overloaded in (4.31), but the theorem's conclusion explicitly compares hat C with AB. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.31)-(4.32)]
hypotheses: The computation uses a mixed-precision MMA unit satisfying Model 1. The accumulation precision satisfies T>=t and its exponent range contains the input exponent range. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1]

The printed theorem is in the default round-to-nearest version of Model 1. Directed rounding is only covered after replacing u,g_min,U,G_min by 2u,2g_min,2U,2G_min. [PDF p. 3, printed B787, paragraph after eq. (2.4)]

Overflow is excluded from the rounding models. The scale theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)) is chosen to prevent input and accumulation overflow. [PDF pp. 2 and 5, printed B786 and B789, eqs. (2.3) and (3.2)]
Lambda and M have power-of-two diagonal entries, and Theorem 4.1 explicitly requires every element of Lambda A and BM to be bounded in magnitude by theta. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1]

The full preceding scaling construction chooses maximal power-of-two row and column scales, giving theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity and theta/(2||y||_infinity)<mu<=theta/||y||_infinity for nonzero x,y. This inherited lower bound is used in the derivation although it is not restated in Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.15)-(4.17)]

A, B, and the unscaled output are stored in sufficiently high precision to be represented exactly, with no underflow or overflow before scaling or after unscaling. [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, paragraph spanning eq. (3.1)]

For i=0,...,p-1, A^(i)=fl((Lambda A-sum_{k=0}^{i-1}u^k A^(k))/u^i); for j=0,...,p-1, B^(j)=fl((BM-sum_{k=0}^{j-1}u^k B^(k))/u^j). The fl operation rounds to the input format. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.30)]
The retained products are exactly those with i+j<p, and their inner products are computed in the accumulation format. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.31)]

No theorem hypothesis states p>1, an upper bound on p, an upper bound on m,n,q, or a smallness condition such as nU<1. Only conforming dimensions and the structurally implicit positive word and inner dimensions occur. [PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed B792 and B795, multiword definition and Theorem 4.1]

The estimates (4.18)-(4.28) are conclusions of the preceding derivation or imported analysis, not assumptions of Theorem 4.1. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, phrases 'we have therefore proven', 'we obtain', and 'In conclusion we have proven']
conclusions: Derived decomposition (4.18): A=sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i Lambda^(-1)A^(i)+Delta A and ||Delta A||_infinity<=zeta||A||_infinity. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.18)]
Derived decomposition (4.19): B=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}u^j B^(j)M^(-1)+Delta B and ||Delta B||_infinity<=zeta||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.19)]
Definition (4.20): zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min). [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.20)]
Proof representation (4.21): hat C=Lambda^(-1)(sum_{i+j<p}u^(i+j)A^(i)B^(j)+Delta C)M^(-1). [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.21)]

Proof rewrite (4.22): the triangular sum is replaced by sum_{i=0}^{p-1}sum_{j=0}^{p-1}u^(i+j)A^(i)B^(j)-sum_{i+j>=p}u^(i+j)A^(i)B^(j), with Delta C retained inside the outer scalings; the second sum has the same implicit 0,...,p-1 index limits. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.22)]
Proof factorization (4.23): hat C=(sum_i u^i Lambda^(-1)A^(i))(sum_j u^j B^(j)M^(-1))+Lambda^(-1)(Delta C-sum_{i+j>=p}u^(i+j)A^(i)B^(j))M^(-1). [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.23)]
Exact error decomposition (4.24): hat C=(A-Delta A)(B-Delta B)+Lambda^(-1)Delta C M^(-1)-sum_{i+j>=p}u^(i+j)Lambda^(-1)A^(i)B^(j)M^(-1). [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.24)]
Definition of total forward error (4.25): hat C=AB+E. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.25)]
Omitted-product estimate (4.26): ||sum_{i+j>=p}u^(i+j)Lambda^(-1)A^(i)B^(j)M^(-1)||_infinity lesssim (p-1)u^p||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.26)]

Accumulation estimate as printed in (4.27): ||Delta C||_infinity lesssim ((n+p^2)U+4rn theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity, where r<=np(p+1)/2 bounds the maximum underflows in any output coefficient. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.27) and following sentence]
Combined estimate (4.28): ||E||_infinity lesssim (2zeta+zeta^2+(p-1)u^p+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.28)]

Theorem 4.1 conclusion (4.32): ||hat C-AB||_infinity lesssim ((p+1)u^p + 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min + (n+p^2)U + 2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. These are exactly the four displayed coefficient terms. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]

Range-unrestricted comparison (4.33): ||hat C-AB||_infinity lesssim ((p+1)u^p+(n+p^2)U)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. It is a cited comparison that omits range limitations, not an additional narrow-range error term. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.33)]

Relative to (4.33), the additional terms in (4.32) are the input-underflow term of order u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min and the accumulation-underflow term of order theta^(-2)G_min. [PDF p. 12, printed B796, first paragraph]

The paper's qualitative conclusion is that multiword arithmetic reduces the input-format rounding and underflow terms by the same order-u^(p-1) factor, while sufficiently large p can leave accumulation-format errors dominant. [PDF p. 12, printed B796, comparison following eq. (4.33)]
definitions_and_conventions: u=2^(-t), f_min=2^(e_min), and f_max=2^(e_max)(2-2u); U=2^(-T), F_min=2^(E_min), and F_max=2^(E_max)(2-2U). [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1]
g_min=f_min/2 without subnormals and g_min=u f_min with gradual underflow; G_min=F_min/2 without subnormals and G_min=U F_min with gradual underflow. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eqs. (2.1)-(2.2)]

theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)); f_max limits input magnitudes and sqrt(F_max/n) limits an n-term accumulation whose two scaled factors are bounded by theta. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, discussion and eq. (3.2)]
The scaled p-word convention is w+Delta w=sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i w^(i), rather than the unweighted sum used by the ordinary decomposition. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed B792-B793, eqs. (4.3)-(4.4)]

Absolute-value vector and matrix inequalities in the decomposition analysis are componentwise, and max in (4.8)-(4.20) is componentwise before conversion to a matrix norm. [PDF pp. 5 and 10, printed B789 and B794, text after eq. (3.6) and before eq. (4.14)]
r is a proof count bounding accumulation underflows in any one output coefficient, with r<=np(p+1)/2. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, paragraph after eq. (4.27)]

The symbol lesssim is used for a simplified or orderwise estimate after higher-order terms have been suppressed; the paper does not define it as a quantified mathematical relation. [PDF p. 7, printed B791, sentence before eq. (3.26); PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.26)-(4.33)]
implicit_context: Theorem 4.1 extends the single-word scaling analysis and therefore relies on the section 3 power-of-two scaling and exact high-precision pre/post-storage context. [PDF pp. 4-5 and 11, printed B788-B789 and B795, eqs. (3.1)-(3.4) and introduction to Theorem 4.1]

The derivation uses lambda^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||x||_infinity and its column analogue, which follow from maximal scaling (3.4), not from the theorem's weaker standalone phrase 'bounded by theta'. [PDF pp. 5 and 10, printed B789 and B794, eqs. (3.4) and (4.15)-(4.17)]

The residual expressions inside fl in (4.29)-(4.30) are written as composite exact arguments followed by one input-format rounding; separate rounding of their subtractions, sums, or divisions is not specified. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.30)]

The paper imports the order-(n+p^2)U accumulation analysis from Fasi et al. and adds its underflow count; it does not state that estimate as an independent hypothesis. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, paragraph before eq. (4.27)]
The conventional empty sum for i=0 or j=0 must be zero for (4.29)-(4.30), although the paper does not state that convention explicitly. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.30)]
The discussion explicitly applies beyond p=1, but Theorem 4.1 itself imposes no p>1 condition. [PDF p. 12, printed B796, sentence ending 'even when p>1'; PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The actual selected algorithm consists of the power-of-two scaling, the p input-format residual-rounding recurrences (4.29)-(4.30), and the triangular weighted product sum (4.31), whose matrix-product inner products use the accumulation format. The actual output is hat C. Delta A, Delta B, zeta, Delta C, r, E, the full p-by-p completion, and the omitted-product sum in (4.18)-(4.28) are proof devices or derived estimates, not extra computed stages or theorem assumptions. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.18)-(4.32)]
numerical_model: Input rounding uses fl(x)=x(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, and eta delta=0, assuming no overflow. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.3)]

Accumulation operations use FL(x op y)=(x op y)(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=U, |eta|<=G_min, eta delta=0, and op in {+,-,multiplication,division}, assuming no overflow. [PDF p. 3, printed B787, eq. (2.4)]

The relative rounding error and additive underflow error are mutually exclusive for each rounded operation, rather than simultaneously accumulated in the same operation. [PDF p. 3, printed B787, paragraph after eq. (2.4)]

Round-to-nearest is the default. The constants in Theorem 4.1 are therefore the round-to-nearest constants unless the model parameters are doubled as prescribed for directed rounding. [PDF p. 3, printed B787, rounding-mode paragraph]
The input format is nested in the accumulation format through T>=t and [E_min,E_max] containing [e_min,e_max]. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1]

Power-of-two scaling and sufficiently high-precision outer storage are treated as exact, subject to the stated absence of underflow and overflow outside the MMA computation. [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, scaling paragraph around eq. (3.1)]
error_notions: Delta A and Delta B are normwise errors of the computed weighted word decompositions, bounded by zeta times the corresponding input norm. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.18)-(4.20)]
Delta C aggregates errors arising while computing the retained A^(i)B^(j) contributions in the accumulation format. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, sentence before eq. (4.21)]
E is the total absolute forward error defined by hat C=AB+E. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.25)]

The final theorem is normwise and absolute: it bounds ||hat C-AB||_infinity by a coefficient times ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. It is not stated as a componentwise bound or as a quotient. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]

The four final sources are input-format rounding, input underflow, accumulation-format rounding, and accumulation underflow, in that order in (4.32). [PDF pp. 11-12, printed B795-B796, eq. (4.32) and comparison after eq. (4.33)]
norms: For vectors x and y, ||.||_infinity is the maximum absolute component, as shown by the scaling intervals based on the maximum row or column coefficient. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, discussion before eq. (3.2) and eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b)]

For matrices, the paper uses ||.||_infinity as a matrix infinity norm in its normwise bounds. The derivation and standard numerical-linear-algebra convention indicate the induced maximum-row-sum norm, but the paper does not explicitly write its formula. [PDF pp. 6-7, printed B790-B791, eqs. (3.23)-(3.24); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]

Entrywise absolute-value inequalities and componentwise max bounds precede conversion to the matrix infinity norm. [PDF pp. 5 and 10, printed B789 and B794, text after eq. (3.6) and eqs. (4.15)-(4.20)]

Underflow prevents the paper from retaining a componentwise final bound; the surrounding analysis explicitly characterizes the result as normwise. [PDF p. 8, printed B792, paragraph beginning 'Finally, note that if underflows occur']
constants_and_indexing: Word indices are i,j=0,...,p-1, residual indices are k=0,...,i-1 or k=0,...,j-1, and the algorithm retains precisely i+j<p. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.31)]
There are exactly p(p+1)/2 retained word-pair products. [PDF p. 8, printed B792, paragraph after eq. (4.2)]
The omitted-pair estimate carries the exact displayed coefficient (p-1)u^p. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.26)]
The maximum accumulation-underflow count is r<=np(p+1)/2, producing 2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min after substitution into 4rn theta^(-2)G_min. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.27)-(4.28)]
The first coefficient in (4.32) is exactly (p+1)u^p. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]
The second coefficient in (4.32) is exactly 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]
The third coefficient in (4.32) is exactly (n+p^2)U. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]
The fourth coefficient in (4.32) is exactly 2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]
The comparison (4.33) contains exactly (p+1)u^p+(n+p^2)U and no g_min or G_min terms. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.33)]
higher_order_terms: The paper explicitly explains its lesssim convention locally by describing (3.26) as obtained by dropping second-order terms from an exact <= bound. [PDF p. 7, printed B791, sentence before eq. (3.26)]

Equation (4.28) explicitly contains zeta^2. Equation (4.32) omits zeta^2; using zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min), the inequality 2zeta<=2u^p+4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min and addition of (p-1)u^p explain the displayed (p+1)u^p and 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min terms. This is an algebraic reconstruction of the paper's simplification, not an additional stated theorem. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.20), (4.28), and (4.32)]
Equations (4.26)-(4.28) already use lesssim, so factors and higher-order contributions hidden there are not enumerated by the paper. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.26)-(4.28)]

Neither (4.32) nor (4.33) supplies an explicit big-O remainder, a hidden constant, its parameter dependence, or a threshold under which the omitted terms are valid. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.32)-(4.33)]

Consequently, replacing lesssim by literal <= with the displayed right-hand side would strengthen the source claim and add semantics absent from the paper. [PDF p. 7, printed B791, introduction to eq. (3.26); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]
exceptional_values: The theorem operates on real matrices and the rounding models assume overflow does not occur. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.3); PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1]
The theta scaling is specifically selected to avoid overflow in both input conversion and n-term accumulation. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, discussion and eq. (3.2)]
Underflow is allowed and modeled in both flush/no-subnormal and gradual-underflow cases through g_min and G_min. [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eqs. (2.1)-(2.2)]

NaNs, infinities, saturation, signed zeros, and their propagation are not part of Model 1 or Theorem 4.1's claim; the proof assumes finite real arithmetic satisfying (2.3)-(2.4). [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, Model 1 and eqs. (2.3)-(2.4)]
The inherited exact-storage assumption excludes underflow and overflow before Lambda,M scaling and after Lambda^(-1),M^(-1) unscaling. [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, paragraph spanning eq. (3.1)]

undebatable_constraints: The exact target is the real product AB of A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x q), and the result concerns the computed hat C. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1 and eq. (4.32)]
The applicable arithmetic is Model 1 with nested input and accumulation formats and distinct parameters u,g_min and U,G_min. [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, Model 1 and eqs. (2.1)-(2.4)]
The printed constants assume round-to-nearest; directed rounding requires the paper's stated doubling substitution. [PDF p. 3, printed B787, rounding-mode paragraph]
Overflow is excluded, while underflow is explicitly included. [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, eqs. (2.3)-(2.4)]
The selected scale is theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)), using diagonal power-of-two factors. [PDF pp. 5 and 11, printed B789 and B795, eq. (3.2) and Theorem 4.1]

The full derivation requires maximal row and column scaling satisfying the factor-of-two lower bounds in (3.4), not merely arbitrary scaled entries below theta. [PDF pp. 5 and 10, printed B789 and B794, eqs. (3.4) and (4.15)-(4.17)]
The word-generation algorithm is the scaled-residual variant (4.29)-(4.30), not the ordinary unweighted decomposition (4.1). [PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed B792 and B795, eqs. (4.1), (4.29), and (4.30)]
Only pairs i+j
Inner products in every retained A^(i)B^(j) are computed in the accumulation format. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, sentence after eq. (4.31)]
Equations (4.18)-(4.28) are proof-derived decompositions and estimates, not hypotheses or additional algorithm stages. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.18)-(4.28)]
The final narrow-range coefficient has exactly four displayed terms: (p+1)u^p, 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min, (n+p^2)U, and 2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)]
The range-free comparison has exactly the first rounding term and the accumulation-rounding term: (p+1)u^p+(n+p^2)U. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.33)]

The final claim is a normwise forward-error lesssim estimate, not a literal displayed <= theorem and not a componentwise result. [PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed B792 and B795, normwise discussion and eq. (4.32)]

No explicit theorem restriction requires p>1, theta>=1, bounded m or q, or a smallness condition on nU or pU. Such conditions must not be added silently. [PDF pp. 11-12, printed B795-B796, Theorem 4.1 and following discussion]

ambiguities.issue: The lesssim relation has no formal semantics in the paper.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper calls a prior lesssim bound a simplification obtained by dropping second-order terms, while (4.26)-(4.33) use the symbol without defining a constant, asymptotic variable, uniformity domain, or remainder. [PDF p. 7, printed B791, sentence before eq. (3.26); PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.26)-(4.33)]
ambiguities.impact: A faithful formalization cannot replace lesssim by <=, choose constant 1, or assert a conventional big-O statement without adding semantics. It must preserve an abstract approximate-bound relation or supply an explicitly acknowledged strengthening.

ambiguities.issue: The standalone wording of Theorem 4.1 understates the scaling condition used by its proof.
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem only says that elements of Lambda A and BM are bounded by theta, but the derivation uses lambda^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||x||_infinity and the analogous mu bound, which require the maximal intervals (3.4). [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.15)-(4.17) and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: Arbitrarily small power-of-two scales satisfy the theorem's literal upper-bound wording but invalidate the displayed underflow coefficient. A formal contract should either inherit (3.4) explicitly or record the theorem's statement/proof gap.

ambiguities.issue: Zero rows or columns are not covered cleanly by the maximal scaling formulas.
ambiguities.evidence: The intervals in (3.4) divide by ||x||_infinity and ||y||_infinity, while Theorem 4.1 quantifies over arbitrary real matrices and supplies no zero-row or zero-column case. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization needs a separate arbitrary nonzero power-of-two scale for zero rows or columns, or must restrict the interval condition to nonzero rows and columns. The paper does not select one.

ambiguities.issue: The exact operational rounding of the residual recurrences and outer word-product sum is underspecified.
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.29)-(4.30) place one fl around a composite residual quotient, and (4.31) explicitly specifies only that inner products in A^(i)B^(j) use the accumulation format. It does not separately specify rounding for residual summation, division, weighting by u^(i+j), summation across word products, or final unscaling. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.31)]
ambiguities.impact: Treating each internal operation as separately rounded defines a different algorithm. The source-level mathematical reading is exact evaluation of each fl argument followed by one rounding, with accumulation effects aggregated as in the proof, but a hardware-level operation sequence cannot be recovered uniquely.

ambiguities.issue: Delta C has a scaling inconsistency in the printed derivation.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.21) places Delta C inside Lambda^(-1)(... )M^(-1), and (4.24) consequently contains Lambda^(-1)Delta C M^(-1). Equation (4.27), however, is printed with ||Delta C||_infinity on the left while its right side is expressed using the unscaled ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.21) and (4.24); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.27)]
ambiguities.impact: The paper likely intends a bound on the externally scaled accumulation error, but the authoritative printed notation does not say so. A formalization must not silently change the left side without recording this discrepancy.

ambiguities.issue: The matrix infinity norm is conventional but not explicitly defined.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper identifies a choice of matrix norm and then writes ||.||_infinity, while separately using vector infinity norms for maximum coefficients; no formula for the matrix norm is printed. [PDF pp. 5-7, printed B789-B791, eqs. (3.4) and (3.23)-(3.24)]
ambiguities.impact: The derivation supports the standard induced maximum-row-sum norm, but a formal statement must define that norm explicitly rather than leaving the symbol polymorphic.

ambiguities.issue: p and matrix-dimension domains are implicit rather than quantified with explicit restrictions.
ambiguities.evidence: p is called the number of words and appears in ranges 0,...,p-1; n appears in sqrt(F_max/n). Theorem 4.1 states no positivity, integrality, upper bounds, or smallness assumptions. [PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed B792 and B795, multiword definition and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: Positive integer p and positive inner dimension n are structurally necessary, but restrictions such as p>1, nU<1, or bounded dimensions would be additions not licensed by the source.

ambiguities.issue: Exceptional IEEE-style values and saturation behavior are outside the theorem model.
ambiguities.evidence: Model 1 states real rounding equations under absence of overflow and Theorem 4.1 uses that model; it does not specify NaN, infinity, saturation, or signed-zero behavior. [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, Model 1 and eqs. (2.3)-(2.4); PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: The contract applies only to finite real executions satisfying Model 1. Extending it to exceptional-value semantics would require assumptions not present in the theorem.

contract_plain_english: For conforming real matrices A and B and an implicitly positive integer word count p, use the nested input and accumulation formats of Model 1, with round-to-nearest, no overflow, and underflow modeled by g_min and G_min. [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, Model 1 and eqs. (2.1)-(2.4)] Scale rows and columns by maximal powers of two so their largest magnitudes lie within a factor of two of theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)); the theorem only restates the upper bound, but the proof requires the lower factor-of-two condition. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.2) and (3.4); PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1] Generate p weighted words by input-format rounding of the scaled residual quotients in (4.29)-(4.30), compute only the p(p+1)/2 products with i+j<p, and compute their inner products in the accumulation format; hat C is the resulting computed output and AB is exact. [PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed B792 and B795, multiword description and eqs. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.18)-(4.32)] Without range limitations, the cited comparison retains only (p+1)u^p+(n+p^2)U. [PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.33)] The lesssim symbol is informal and suppresses higher-order terms, including the explicit zeta^2 present in (4.28); the paper supplies no constant or remainder semantics that would justify replacing it by a literal inequality.
